speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about your fatigue and lower leg swelling, such as how long these symptoms have been present? Also, has the weight loss been intentional or unintentional?

speaker: Patient
text: 66-year-old white male. The patient reports a 10-day history of fatigue and bilateral lower leg swelling. He mentions a weight loss of 3.6 kg (8 lbs) over the past 6 months without trying. He has a history of chronic bronchitis and uses an albuterol inhaler as needed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any shortness of breath or difficulty breathing when lying flat or during exertion? I also need to know if you have noticed any abdominal swelling, loss of appetite, or changes in your bowel habits.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any shortness of breath, chest pain, or palpitations, and have you noticed any changes in your urine output or foamy urine? I would also like to know if you have a history of diabetes, high blood pressure, or kidney disease.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Chronic bronchitis. Social history: History of smoking one pack of cigarettes daily for 44 years and drinks one alcoholic beverage daily.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal venous duplex rules out deep vein thrombosis, suggesting the leg swelling is likely due to right heart strain or hypoalbuminemia secondary to the malignancy. I will assess your cardiac function and nutritional status. REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram REQUEST TEST: Serum_Albumin

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of 4+ protein in the urine indicates nephrotic syndrome, which is the cause of your severe hypoalbuminemia and subsequent leg swelling. Given the lung mass and these findings, this is likely a paraneoplastic manifestation such as membranous nephropathy associated with your lung cancer. DIAGNOSIS READY: Lung Cancer with Paraneoplastic Membranous Nephropathy
